Stability conditions on synthetic fixture surfaces

A. Fixture
Abstract.

We construct a two-section synthetic document whose theorem, lemma, definition, and proof environments carry the native-render class vocabulary, pinning chunker compatibility with the arxiv.org/html surface.

1 Stability functions

Let XX be a smooth projective surface with bounded derived category Db⁡(X)D^{b}(X).

Definition 1.1.

A stability function on an abelian category 𝒜\mathcal{A} is a group homomorphism Z:K⁡(𝒜)→ℂZ:K(\mathcal{A})\to\mathbb{C} such that every nonzero object has image in the strict upper half-plane union the negative real axis.

Theorem 1.2 (Fixture support property).

Every stability function on the fixture heart 𝒜0\mathcal{A}_{0} satisfies the support property with respect to the quadratic form Q⁡(v)=v2+1Q(v)=v^{2}+1.

Proof.

Positivity is immediate on the fixture heart because the central charge is discrete on the lattice K⁡(𝒜0)K(\mathcal{A}_{0}). The discreteness bound gives the support constant directly. \qedhere

2 Wall-and-chamber structure

The stability manifold of the fixture surface decomposes into chambers cut out by countably many walls.

Lemma 2.1.

Walls for a fixed class vv are locally finite in the fixture stability manifold.

Proof.

Each wall is determined by a class of bounded norm; the support property bounds the norm by Q⁡(v)\sqrt{Q(v)}, and classes of bounded norm form a finite set in each compact region.
